1.6 Metadata extraction and categories

The comparison invokes ExifTool once per pending batch, overlapping extraction with image work. It requests JSON, grouped/instance-qualified names, numeric output, structured values, unknown tags and binary contents. Preview/raw image payloads are excluded because the image comparator reads those directly. The portable snapshot route additionally retains the wider grouped output described under metadata archives.

ExifTool’s JSON and grouping options are important: structured XMP and binary values can be retained instead of a flattened presentation or a byte-count placeholder. The tool’s numeric output is its own representation of metadata; Python does not recover the original TIFF storage type from that JSON. ExifTool’s application documentation.

The main comparator normalizes global CopyN group numbering so adding one XMP field does not make unchanged EXIF duplicate instances appear changed. Real duplicate values within a group remain retained. It flattens dictionaries for field comparison and labels differences directionally:

  • added: present on the right and absent on the left.
  • removed: present on the left and absent on the right.
  • changed: present on both sides with unequal values.

It separates embedded, filesystem and layout. Directory, filename, access time, ExifTool’s own fields and derived Composite fields are excluded from this comparison. File size, modification/change time and permissions can appear as filesystem differences. TIFF image offsets/counts and preview placement belong to layout. A layout difference need not change samples.

Metadata comparison covers what ExifTool exposes under the chosen flags. It does not compare all arbitrary padding, unused bytes or uninterpreted private structures. Warnings and errors are retained. In the compact Python report, large differing values have a canonical JSON length, SHA-256 and prefix instead of the full printed value. The portable gzip archive retains full extracted values for later queries or restoration decisions.
